To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IL 6 type signalling involves the assembly of receptor heterotrimers, which activate Janus kinases, which in turn phosphorylate STAT proteins, which then dimerize, are translocated to the nucleus, bind to enhancer sequences, and thereby activate target gene transcription.
IL 6, IL11, leukaemic inhibitory factor, cardiotrophin and oncostatin M signal through the gp 130/Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription pathway.
cytokines of the IL 2, IL 3, IL 4 and IL 6 type signal through the Jaks and STATs to induce the expression of target genes.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pleiotropic functions of the IL 16 type cytokines and the development of new strategies to modulate these cytokines and their signalling.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of the IL 16 type cytokine signal transduction.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of signal transduction of IL 6 and its family members and their physiological role.

the IL 6 cytokines signal through a common receptor complex, which is composed of gp130 and one specific receptor subunit.
the IL 6-type cytokines have a common signalling mechanism, but different functions in vivo.

IL 6 and IL 11 are involved in bone formation and repair; oncostatin M in the regulation of cell differentiation and apoptosis; and cardiotrophins and leukaemia inhibiting factor in the regulation of the heart and the nervous system, respectively.
IL 6 type signalling is a highly regulated process, which involves the concerted action of various proteins, and that the signalling is terminated in a timely and controlled manner.

the IL 6 family of cytokines is a very important group of cytokines that are involved in a wide range of biological processes.
the IL 6 cytokine family has evolved a common signalling pathway, which is utilized by the individual cytokines to induce distinct cellular responses.
